steps.question: Which genes in blood show significant treatment vs control differential expression across the 5 paired subjects, using DESeq2 with subject as a blocking factor (design ~ subject + condition)?
acceptance_criteria: Counts.csv (12000 genes x 10 samples) and metadata.csv (10 rows: subject, condition) are loaded and sample order/names are matched between the two files

Standard DESeq2 QC produced: library size barplot, PCA on rlog/vst-transformed counts colored by subject and by condition, and a sample-sample distance heatmap to confirm no mislabeling or outlier sample

steps.name: Per-subject paired log2 fold-change and directional concordance across subjects
caveats: Do not report per-subject per-gene p-values from n=1 pairs — there is no statistical basis for a p-value with zero degrees of freedom at the single-gene, single-subject level
Use DESeq2 size factors (from T1S1) rather than raw counts, since library sizes can differ between control/treated samples within a subject
steps.question: For each of the 5 subjects individually, which genes show the largest treated-vs-control log2 fold change from that subject's single control-treated pair, and how many of the 5 subjects show each gene moving in the same direction (concordance)?
acceptance_criteria: For each subject, paired log2 fold-change computed per gene as log2((treated_count+1)/(control_count+1)) using size-factor-normalized counts (reuse DESeq2 size factors from T1S1) to correct for sequencing depth differences between the paired samples
A subject x gene matrix of normalized paired log2FC values is produced (5 subjects x ~12000 genes)

For each gene, a concordance score is computed: number/fraction of the 5 subjects with log2FC in the same direction (sign) and above a minimal magnitude threshold (e.g., |log2FC| > 1), distinguishing genes with uniform within-subject response from genes with subject-specific or discordant response
Top genes ranked by concordance and mean magnitude are reported in a table, explicitly separating 'consistent across subjects' genes from 'discordant/heterogeneous' genes

Caveat stated in the output that per-subject single-pair log2FC has no within-subject replicate to estimate technical/biological noise, so these are descriptive effect-size rankings, not gene-level hypothesis tests

steps.name: Per-subject pathway-level deregulation (N-of-1-style) using WikiPathways human gene sets
caveats: If WikiPathways gene symbol coverage against the 12000-gene panel is low (e.g., <50% of pathway genes matched), report the coverage explicitly rather than silently proceeding
fgsea nominal p-values from single-subject rankings are noisier than cohort-level GSEA; do not apply the same significance threshold conventions without flagging this
steps.question: Which WikiPathways human pathways show coherent up- or down-regulation within each individual subject's single control-treated pair, and do these per-subject deregulated pathways converge across subjects more than the individual genes do?
acceptance_criteria: WikiPathways human gene sets (GMT, HGNC symbols) loaded and matched to the ~12000 gene symbols in the count matrix, reporting the fraction of pathway genes found in the dataset

For each subject, the per-subject paired log2FC vector from T2S1 is used to rank genes and run a pre-ranked gene set enrichment analysis (fgsea) per subject-pathway pair (mirrors N-of-1-pathways framework of Gardeux et al. 2014 JAMIA and Schissler et al. 2018 Stat Methods Med Res, which uses paired single-subject transcriptomes with gene set structure to gain statistical traction that individual genes lack)
A subject x pathway matrix of normalized enrichment scores (NES) and per-subject BH-adjusted p-values is produced

Pathways ranked by how many of the 5 subjects reach nominal significance (e.g., padj<0.25 per fgsea convention for single-sample-derived rankings) are reported, separating pathways deregulated consistently across most/all subjects from those private to one or two subjects

Report explicitly states that per-subject NES from a single pair is a descriptive/exploratory signal, not a population-level inferential claim, consistent with the N-of-1-pathways literature's own limitations

steps.name: Pathway enrichment of the population-level paired DE genes
caveats: If very few genes pass padj<0.05 given n=5, fall back to reporting the pre-ranked fgsea result on the full gene list rather than an empty over-representation test
steps.question: Which WikiPathways human pathways are enriched among genes significantly differentially expressed between treated and control across the 5-subject paired cohort (from T1S1)?
acceptance_criteria: WikiPathways human GMT loaded and gene universe restricted to the ~12000 genes tested in T1S1
Over-representation analysis (or fgsea pre-ranked on the full DESeq2 stat/LFC) run on the T1S1 significant gene set (padj<0.05) against WikiPathways pathways
Enriched pathways reported with adjusted p-values and the leading-edge/member gene overlap with the DE gene list

Result cross-referenced against the per-subject pathway concordance table from T2S2 to note whether population-significant pathways are also the ones showing multi-subject concordance, or whether they diverge

plan.title: Paired within-subject treatment DE analysis (n=5)
plan.analytical_narrative: The data are raw STAR/featureCounts gene-level counts (12000 genes x 10 samples) from 5 subjects, each contributing a matched control and treated blood sample — a fully paired design. The research question ('which genes respond to treatment within each subject') has two legitimate readings that the plan addresses in sequence: (1) the standard cohort-level paired DE test, which uses subject as a blocking factor in DESeq2 to find genes that respond to treatment consistently across the 5 subjects while removing inter-subject variance, and (2) genuine per-subject (N-of-1 style) DE, since the design gives exactly one control-treated pair per subject and the question explicitly asks 'within each subject'. Standard per-gene hypothesis testing from a single pair has essentially no power (df=0 per subject at the gene level), so subject-level differential signal is instead assessed at the pathway/gene-set level using paired log-fold-change ranking per subject against WikiPathways human gene sets — the approach validated in the N-of-1-pathways literature (Gardeux et al. 2014 JAMIA; Schissler et al. 2018 Stat Methods Med Res) for exactly this two-sample-per-patient setting. Track 1 produces the population-level paired DESeq2 result (genes responding to treatment on average, adjusting for subject). Track 2 produces per-subject deregulated gene lists (simple paired log2FC ranking per subject, since no replicate exists within a subject to estimate per-gene variance) and per-subject pathway enrichment, plus a concordance analysis (how many of the 5 subjects show each gene/pathway moving in the same direction) to distinguish uniform responders from heterogeneous ones. This concordance step is the direct, defensible answer to 'which genes respond within each subject' beyond the population-average model.
